list.name: Restarts
list.textFormat: process_start_time_seconds changed (crash, OOM kill or kill-service)

list.name: Flag flips
list.textFormat: runtime flag switched from the control plane

description: RED (rate, errors, duration) and USE-style saturation for every Node service, plus outbound dependency health (HTTP client outcomes, retries, circuit breakers) and restarts. Pick services with the selector.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Inbound requests per second per service (probes excluded). Fan-out amplification shows up here: one gateway request can become several catalog / cart / inventory requests (lab n-plus-one, cart.pricing=per_item_calls).

panels.title: 5xx error ratio
panels.description: Share of responses that are 5xx per service. Dashed line: 5% (ServiceErrorRateHigh). Follow errors downstream with the HTTP client panels below: the failing service is usually the one whose dependencies fail.

targets.expr:
(
  sum by (service) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready", status=~"5.."}[30s]))
  or
  0 * sum by (service) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[30s]))
)
/
sum by (service) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[30s]))

panels.title: Error responses by code
panels.description: Error responses per service by the error code in the body (http_server_errors_total): business answers (OUT_OF_STOCK, QUEUE_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, BOT_SUSPECTED...) next to real failures (INTERNAL, INJECTED_FAULT, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, in red).

panels.title: Latency p50
panels.description: p50 latency per service from http_server_request_duration_seconds over 30s. Typical request.

panels.title: Latency p95
panels.description: p95 latency per service from http_server_request_duration_seconds over 30s. One in twenty requests is slower than this.

panels.title: Latency p99
panels.description: p99 latency per service from http_server_request_duration_seconds over 30s. Tail latency: where queueing, lock waits and timeouts show up first.

panels.title: In-flight requests
panels.description: Concurrent requests per service. Little's law: concurrency = throughput x latency. Rising in-flight at steady traffic means requests are waiting on something (a pool, a lock, a slow dependency).

panels.title: Non-2xx responses by status
panels.description: Responses that are not 2xx, by service and HTTP status. 5xx in red.

panels.title: Routes (last 1m)
panels.description: Per-route RED summary. Sort by p99 or 5xx to find the worst endpoint, then look at its dependencies.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[1m])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service, route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[1m])))

(
  sum by (service, route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready", status=~"5.."}[1m]))
  or
  0 * sum by (service, route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[1m]))
)
/
sum by (service, route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service", route!~"/metrics|/health|/ready"}[1m]))

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: p99 delay of the event loop. Everything on a Node process shares this single thread. Dashed: 200ms (EventLoopLagHigh). Labs: logging-meltdown (synchronous console.log), gc-pauses, overload-collapse.

panels.title: Event loop lag max
panels.description: Longest single stall per scrape. Periodic spikes with a flat p99 = stop-the-world pauses (lab gc-pauses). A stall longer than 2s also makes the scrape time out (up == 0).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used per service; 100% = one full core. Node executes JavaScript on one thread, so ~100% is the ceiling and latency climbs steeply before you get there.

panels.title: Resident memory (RSS)
panels.description: Process memory as the kernel sees it. Containers are limited to 512 MiB (dashed line; loadgen 1.5 GiB): crossing it means an OOM kill and a restart. Steady growth with no plateau is a leak — lab memory-leak.

panels.title: Heap used & external memory
panels.description: V8 heap in use (JS objects) and external memory (Buffers, off-heap). If RSS grows but heap does not, the leak is outside the JS heap. Heap is capped at 384 MiB by --max-old-space-size.

panels.title: Memory growth rate
panels.description: Slope of RSS over 5 minutes (bytes per second). A healthy service hovers around 0 after warm-up; a sustained positive slope predicts the OOM kill. MemoryGrowing fires above 200 KiB/s for 2 minutes.

panels.title: Time in GC
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time spent in garbage collection, by GC kind (minor = scavenge, major = mark-sweep-compact). More than ~10% means allocation pressure is eating your latency budget. Lab: gc-pauses.

panels.title: GC runs per second
panels.description: How often the collector runs. Frequent minor GCs are normal under load; frequent major GCs indicate a heap that keeps growing.

panels.title: Active handles
panels.description: Open handles (sockets, timers, file descriptors) per process. With keep-alive off every service-to-service call opens a new socket, so handle counts churn and CPU rises from connection setup. Lab: connection-churn.

panels.title: Calls by target
panels.description: Outbound calls per second, caller -> target (each logical call, including its retries).

panels.title: Failed calls by outcome
panels.description: Calls that did not end ok: http_error (5xx from the target), timeout, network_error (connection refused/reset) and circuit_open (failed fast by the breaker — cheap, and the reason breakers exist).

panels.title: Call latency p99 by target
panels.description: p99 of outbound calls including retries. A slow non-critical dependency with a 30s timeout makes every caller wait 30s (lab cascading-failure).

panels.title: Retries per second
panels.description: Retries issued per caller -> target. Immediate retries of everything multiply load exactly when the target is weakest. Lab: retry-storm.

panels.title: Retry amplification
panels.description: Retries per call over 1m. 0.1 = 10% extra load from retries (a sane budget). With naive_immediate retries and a failing target this can exceed 2-3x. Dashed: 20% (RetryStorm).

targets.expr:
sum by (service, target) (rate(http_client_retries_total{service=~"$service"}[1m]))
/
sum by (service, target) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service"}[1m]))

panels.title: Circuit breaker state
panels.description: 0 closed (calls flow), 1 half-open (probing), 2 open (failing fast).

panels.title: Breaker transitions & retry budget
panels.description: Breaker transitions per minute by destination state, and retries refused because the retry budget was empty (the hardened policy protecting a struggling dependency).

panels.title: TCP connections opened/s by target
panels.description: New TCP connections each caller opens to each target per second (http_client_connections_opened_total). With keep-alive the pool warms up once and this falls to ~0; with platform.keepAlive=off every call pays a handshake and the line tracks the call rate. Lab: connection-churn.

panels.title: New connections per call
panels.description: Connections opened / calls made over 1m. ~0 = sockets are reused; ~1 or more = a new connection for every call (retries open more). Dashed: 0.5, the ConnectionChurn alert threshold.

targets.expr:
sum by (service, target) (rate(http_client_connections_opened_total{service=~"$service"}[1m]))
/
sum by (service, target) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{service=~"$service"}[1m]))

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Scrape health per service. DOWN = process dead, restarting, or its event loop blocked past the 2s scrape timeout.

panels.title: Restarts in range
panels.description: Process restarts in the selected time range (changes of process_start_time_seconds). OOM kills from the memory-leak lab and the kill-service action land here.

panels.title: Active chaos
panels.description: Fault injection switched on per service (chaos_active == 1).

panels.title: Gateway admission counter vs real in-flight
panels.description: What the load shedder believes is in flight (gateway_admission_inflight) against what the HTTP server really has in flight. They should track each other. A growing gap means admission slots are leaking — usually a release path that misses client disconnects (lab shedding-death-spiral). 499s are requests whose client hung up first.

panels.title: Shed and abandoned requests
panels.description: Requests shed by reason (inflight limit vs queueing delay) and requests whose client disconnected before the response (status 499).
